question.prompt: A box contains chips, each of which is red, white, or blue. The number of blue chips is at least half the number of white chips and at most one-third the number of red chips. The number which are white or blue is at least \(55.\) The minimum number of red chips is:

solutions.explanation:
Let \(W,B,R\) be the nonnegative integer counts of white, blue, and red chips. The conditions give
\[
W\le2B,\qquad R\ge3B,\qquad W+B\ge55.
\]
To make the red count small, first find how small the blue count can be. Since the white count is at most twice the blue count,
\[
55\le W+B\le3B.
\]
Thus \(B\ge55/3\). Because chips come in whole numbers, \(B\ge19\), so
\[
R\ge3B\ge57.
\]

A lower bound is a minimum only if it can be attained. Take \(W=36\), \(B=19\), and \(R=57\). Then \(19\ge36/2\), \(19=57/3\), and \(36+19=55\), so every condition holds. Therefore the minimum red count is \(\boxed{57}\), choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
solutions.title: Bound the blue count, then attain the red bound
